title: Asymmetric dependency degradation: progressive circuit-breaker and tenant-priority chaos run
creator: Ava Kim
description: Background: We observed intermittent, region-specific degradations from an internal lookup service (prefix-cache) that only affects a subset of tenants (due to tenant-aware routing in the dependency). These asymmetric failures cause skewed SLO violations: some tenants see high tail latency and retries while others are unaffected. Previous chaos runs focused on full-region blackholes or GPU exhaustion uniformly across tenants; this ticket targets a targeted, partial-degradation scenario and validates progressive circuit-breaker behavior + tenant-priority load-shedding so customer-impact is minimized.
test_plan: 1) Create a proxy shim that can inject partial degradation (increased latency and 10-30% error rate) to prefix-cache for region-us-east and only for tenant clusters A/B. 2) Simulate GPU pool pressure in us-east to force throttling + longer queue times on serving nodes concurrently. 3) Configure progressive circuit breaker thresholds on runtime routing knobs: soft trip at P95 latency, hard trip at P99 and error rate > 5%. 4) Add tenant-priority load-shedding policy: premium tenants bypass initial shed; standard tenants shed at soft trip; best-effort shed at hard trip. 5) Run canary with synthetic traffic for 30m, then ramp to 3x baseline for 1h. 6) Observe routing: ensure failover to us-west is triggered for tripped flows, ensure KV-prefix fallback path is used for shed traffic where possible. 7) Record SLIs: P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, successful failover rate, cost delta. 8) Rollback plan: disable injection and revert circuit thresholds to default if regressions exceed safety gates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated partial dependency degradation trips circuit-breakers as expected (soft -> hard) without manual intervention
Failover to secondary region (us-west) completes within configured failover window for affected flows
Tenant-priority load-shedding prevents P99 violations for premium tenants while reducing throughput for best-effort tenants
No sustained SLO regression for global customers beyond 10 minutes during test
observability_checks: Dashboards to monitor during run: SLO heatmap, per-tenant P99, circuit-breaker state timeline, per-region GPU utilization, ingress queue length, KV cache hit ratio. Create Grafana snapshot and recording rule to verify SLI deltas.
safety_gates: Abort run and auto-rollback if overall customer-facing error rate > 3% for 5 consecutive minutes OR if premium-tenant P99 increases by > 50% over baseline for 2 minutes.
